title: Discourse markers B2
note: contrast beyond however (nevertheless, whereas, in contrast, even so, though at the end) · result (consequently, as a result, thus, hence, otherwise, that is why) · addition (moreover, furthermore, in addition, besides, what is more) · sentence adverb vs conjunction vs preposition, the punctuation rule B1 does not cover · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 10)

items.en: The results were poor. Nevertheless, we will try again.
items.cz: Výsledky byly špatné. Přesto to zkusíme znovu.
items.gap: The results were poor. ____, we will try again.
accepts: The results were poor. Nevertheless, we will try again.
items.explanation: These all mark contrast but attach differently: however / nevertheless / in contrast / even so start a new sentence, whereas / while join two clauses, and though can be added at the end.
items.explanation_cz: Všechny vyjadřují kontrast, ale připojují se jinak: however / nevertheless / in contrast / even so začínají novou větu, whereas / while spojují dvě věty a though se dá přidat na konec.

cards.title: Sentence adverb, conjunction or preposition?
cards.body: B1 gave you the meanings. The B2 problem is grammar: each marker demands a particular thing after it, and that decides the punctuation too.
cards.body_cz: Významy znáš z B1. Problém na B2 je gramatický: každý výraz vyžaduje po sobě něco jiného, a to určuje i interpunkci.

table.caption: what follows
rows: sentence adverb
however · nevertheless · therefore · moreover
a new sentence, or a semicolon before it
conjunction
although · even though · because · whereas · while
a full clause (subject + verb)
preposition
despite · in spite of · because of
a noun or -ing form, never a clause

points: The cost was high. However, we bought it. (new sentence)
Although the cost was high, we bought it. (clause)
Despite the high cost, we bought it. (noun)
A sentence adverb after a comma is the commonest B2 error: not `It was expensive, however we bought it.`

cards.title: Contrast beyond however
cards.body: nevertheless is the formal however. in contrast and on the other hand set two things side by side. whereas and while join the two halves into one sentence. though can be tacked onto the end.
cards.body_cz: nevertheless je formální however. in contrast a on the other hand staví dvě věci vedle sebe. whereas a while spojují obě poloviny do jedné věty. though se dá přidat na konec.
points: The results were poor. Nevertheless, we will try again.
She works in sales, whereas her brother works in research.
It was expensive. We bought it, though. (end position, spoken)
however can also sit in the middle between two commas: The new one, however, works well.
even so = despite that fact: The room was cold. Even so, we were happy there.

cards.title: Result: therefore and its relatives
cards.body: therefore, consequently, thus and hence are the formal ones; as a result and that is why are neutral. otherwise is different — it gives the result of NOT doing the first thing.
cards.body_cz: therefore, consequently, thus a hence jsou formální; as a result a that is why jsou neutrální. otherwise je jiné — udává následek toho, když první věc neuděláš.
points: The report arrived late. Consequently, we missed the deadline.
Prices went up quickly; hence we changed our plan.
Book the tickets today. Otherwise, the price will go up.
that is why takes no comma after it: That is why the boss called her.

cards.title: Addition: moreover, furthermore, besides
cards.body: moreover, furthermore, in addition and what is more add a second and usually stronger point — they belong to writing. besides is more spoken and adds a reason that clinches the argument.
cards.body_cz: moreover, furthermore, in addition a what is more přidávají další, obvykle silnější argument — patří do psaného projevu. besides je hovorovější a přidává důvod, který argument uzavírá.
points: The flat is small. Moreover, it is very expensive.
She speaks German. In addition, she knows some French.
It is too expensive. Besides, we do not need it. (spoken)
besides is the adverb; beside means next to — two different words.

cards.title: Common mistakes

table.caption: check
rows: It was expensive, however we bought it.
It was expensive. However, we bought it.
Despite the cost was high, we bought it.
Despite the high cost, we bought it.
Although the high cost, we bought it.
Although the cost was high, we bought it.
In spite of the rain, but the match started.
In spite of the rain, the match started.
Beside, we do not need it.
Besides, we do not need it.
In addition of the pool, there is a gym.
In addition to the pool, there is a gym.

points: Never pair although with but — Czech `přestože… ale` does not carry over.
despite has no of: despite the rain, not `despite of the rain`.
